_comment: GAUSSIAN GOLDEN — every hash below was produced TWICE: once by the pre-EMG parent commit
52e6c91 (which had no --peak-shape flag at all, so it renders the Gaussian by construction),
and once by this tree with `--peak-shape gaussian`. Both runs agreed. tests/golden_gaussian.rs
re-runs the same four writer/mode combinations and re-checks them, so any future drift in the
Gaussian path fails a test instead of silently restating 124 h of cached renders.
WHAT IS HASHED, AND WHY IT IS SPLIT
signal  = the rendered measurement. MUST equal the parent commit byte for byte: this covers
quantisation, zstd compression, frame indexing and the vendor container.
metadata= the provenance stamp this work ADDS (peak shape + k + n_sigma). It is expected to
differ from the parent, and its content is pinned here so the stamp itself cannot
drift either. For analysis.tdf, parent-vs-head equality was verified by comparing
full `sqlite3 .dump` output modulo exactly the three Sim* rows listed below.
Regenerate: tests/golden/regenerate.sh (see that script for the parent-build procedure).
Fixture paths are machine-local; the test SKIPS (loudly) a case whose inputs are absent, and
FAILS if that leaves nothing to check.

Cases pin BOTH --peak-shape gaussian AND --mobility-std-target 0: the first turns off the per-peptide elution shape, the second the per-ion mobility width. Both are needed to reproduce the pre-EMG binary, because per-ion mobility changes the rendered SIGNAL (analysis.tdf_bin), not just metadata -- the only change in this line of work that does.

parent_differs_only_by: Mobility-window drop (2026-08-11): ions whose 1/K0 falls outside the acquisition window are now DROPPED rather than clamped to the edge scan. v2 was depositing their full signal at the ramp edge, inventing peaks the instrument could not record — 3581 of 12228 ions on the fixture, and 5.2% of total ion signal rendered as phantom 1+. v1 has always dropped them (simulator.py:2291). This is a correctness fix, not a modelling toggle, so unlike the peak-shape features it gets no off-switch and the baseline moves.

Frames.Time / rt_seconds: the render now inherits the reference .d's own frame period instead of the hardcoded --cycle-seconds 0.1 default, which had been writing a 5.2%-compressed time axis into a file carrying that reference's own DIA windows and calibration. v1 has always read this off the reference (acquisition.py:177-184). Re-baselined 2026-08-10; analysis.tdf_bin is UNCHANGED and keeps its parent-equality claim, so the rendered signal is unaffected.

Not a writer. It renders into memory to measure throughput and produces no artifact to hash. Its shape/geometry handling is covered by the unit tests in src/render.rs (it shares stream_render_flat and the same validators).
